title: Two members describe the shop the ideal banh mi comes from
summary: Under @shibbi.me's photo of her first banh mi in years (Tue 17 Nov, caption "Yeah it’s all right ig"), @handackett.bsky.social wrote that real ones rarely live up to the ideal in his head, which he traced to a single remembered hole-in-the-wall. @anthonybecker.bsky.social answered with the kind of place one has to buy them from: a business that would rather not sell them because its main product is baguettes. He added "proceed to eat 2-4 of them per week for years", the same figure he had posted about himself earlier in the window, on Fri 13 Nov ("I eat 2-4 banh mi per week btw"). @handackett.bsky.social added that the shop should not look like a legitimate business, and @words.bsky.social agreed in general terms about food and tax status.

sensitive: No post on this card carries a flag from the tool. (1) The exchange continues past the last post here into personal anecdotes that involve drugs; those five posts are left out. (2) The lines about the tax authorities are about an imagined kind of shop, not a named business; nothing here should be attached to a real shop. (3) @handackett.bsky.social has 461 followers: above the digest's small-account line of 300, still a small audience. (4) The wave's origin: Where the banh mi wave came from is not for the show. Other posts in the window by some of the same accounts frame it around trans women, and a thread about it turns to hormone medication and nudes (R10: gender identity, health, sexuality). The digest flags several of those posts one by one, and flags the whole thread "why is everyone banh mi posting?" (story 12, which also holds the "banhmi-contagion" graph the build bot made): nothing from that thread is on this card and the check refuses it. None of this should be used as explanation or background; the show cannot say why the wave started beyond what the posts listed here say.
